Borderlands, shortly after moving in with my cousin I picked up a used copy for 360. I had previously only played it for 20 minutes and he had never played it. We bonded throughout that co-op.

I'm glad you said that. Borderlands had bonded me and my friends during our deployment. After long hours and road trips, we got together on LAN and played for hours, grinding and talking trash. It was the best of times, it was the worst of times, and it was our times.

Final Fantasy 7, i feel i understood more about compassion and respect for life at a rather early age. I still say to this day, it is one of the most eye opening storylines to have existed in recent years. The philosophy behind the story and the characters themselves are nothing but a masterpiece worth playing through.

Spec Ops: The Line made me question my beliefs in government, the military, and patriotism.

World of Warcraft made me meet friends that I've now kept in touch with for almost a decade. We don't play the game anymore but we play many other games together and skype regularly.

Call of Duty 2 had a huge impact in my life. As a kid I grew up near a local LAN center. My parents would drop me off with some friends and we played for hours. When COD 2 came out, I played it like no tomorrow. They formed 2 competitive teams for COD 2 at the center to compete in national tournaments for prizes. A friend and I was able to join the same one. Those are some of the best memories of my childhood. Training, competing, winning, losing. That game introduced me to the competitive side of gaming and I have always had a bug in me since to try and be really good at FPS games. COD 2 made every shooter I played since then something more...something deeper. I still have friends from the tournament teams too. Friends for life.

Skyrim. It might sound silly, but it helped with my transition after losing a love. Not capable of venturing into real nature by myself at that time, I just enjoyed lurking in that beautiful world with beautiful music and over time it I felt better. It had some strange nostalgic-melancholic effect on me :D Kind of cool!

League of Legends inspired me not to be a toxic shitlord to other players. not that I was to begin with, it just further cemented the fact that i didnt want to treat other players like that (in any game).

Final Fantasy IX

It was the first FF game I played and it was when I was in 4th grade. It was the first time that I was exposed to such a complex story of heroes, love, sacrifice, and some meaning of life. I really had fun with it too. It was very profound to me and reading all of the text and immersing myself in the game helped me become a better reader and person overall. I feel like it really opened my mind for the first time.
Same! It was the first FF I played too and helped me through a difficult teenage phase, and it actually taught me a lot about life. Which does sound silly typing it but it's true.
Riven was an obsession for me as a child. I honestly hold that game sacred in a way. The whole Myst series is great but Riven changed my life.

Need for Speed series. I had been playing it obsessively for months, when I stupidly got into a bad traffic situation on the highway. I had to make a very quick decision and because of all the accidents I had in NfS, I calmy and without hesitation plowed into the orange and white barrels, coming to a stop. Any other option would've resulted in an accident, and probably a not pretty one. NfS made me not fear that option, as it felt so normal to crash in that manner.

Not a game, per se, but playing improv games helped me learn a few social golden rules.

Best one to utilize is, "Yes, and".

No matter the circumstances, it allows the performers to continue progressing and playing within any story. Not only, that, but it forces the performers to discover their ability to move in any direction and still gain the upper hand. Kinda like Aikido, where you use the momentum of the attacker to defend yourself.

Pokemon Red/Blue.

Back when I was about 9 or 10, I lived in a predominantly Hispanic neighborhood. Not knowing Spanish, it was easy for kids to pick on me without me being any the wiser to their conversations.

I didn't do well in school and was held back to re take the 5th grade at another school in the district. In that second year of 5th grade, Pokemon Red/Blue came out. I was lucky enough to get it from my parents after they went hunting for it for a few days.

Because of my parents quick actions, I was one of the first kids in my class to have the game, and thus in others knowing that I had the game, they came to me for tips and advice. From there I made a few friends that stuck with me for the rest of the year.

I remember at the end of the school year we had a bowling field trip and me and my group of friends came up with the team name "Poke Pals". That year really helped re establish my self confidence and made the transition to "middle school" much easier.

Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons, if you have not played the game yourself. I fully reccomend you stop reading this, get a controller and a solid afternoon and evening to crank it out. Game really hit home and gave me an appreciation for family that I had, but was strengthened immensely throughout the game itself. A game that has stuck with me and will until I'm in the grave.
Pokemon. If it wasn't for that I would have never got into cock fighting.

Doorkickers has made me a better and more aware driver. For those that aren't aware, it is a top down strategy game where you storm a building with a set number of officers to save hostages or eliminate the terrorists. You plan routes and flashbang locations ahead of time like the Rainbow Six series.

I can't think of any game that demonstrates as effectively as this one how fickle your vision can be and forces you to understand that a person has a set cone of vision. Someone may be moving in between the time after you checked your blind spot and that represents a vulnerability.

Now when I check my blind spots when driving, I understand how long that 'check' is valid for given the speed that we're all going at. Immediately after playing, I notice when I drive I am much more diligent about how observant I am of my surroundings.
